subject.title: fix(config): warn when JSON5 comments are lost on config write

question: Should comment loss become a permanent exported config-write diagnostic, and if so should the API be the proposed singular warning field or an extensible typed diagnostic collection?
rationale: The branch is technically coherent, but repository policy treats exported config APIs and compatibility surfaces as maintainer-owned product contracts; source inspection cannot determine the intended long-term cardinality and semantics.

options.title: Use typed diagnostics
options.body: Replace the two singular warning fields with one typed diagnostic collection, retain quiet-output behavior, and prove it through an actual supported config command.

options.title: Accept singular warning
options.body: Adopt warning?: string as the stable result contract and require public-command proof before merge.

options.title: Keep warning internal
options.body: Limit the change to human-facing logging and avoid adding an exported structured result contract, accepting that quiet callers will not receive the diagnostic.

recommendation.title: Use typed diagnostics
recommendation.body: Replace the two singular warning fields with one typed diagnostic collection, retain quiet-output behavior, and prove it through an actual supported config command.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent adjacent config-write warning history makes this the strongest available owner signal for choosing diagnostic semantics.
